description: Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake has warned crypto holders about a worst-case scenario in which AI-assisted advances could threaten ECDSA security within months. He proposed “bunker mode”, involving gradual transfers to fresh addresses. Vitalik Buterin advised against rushing to move funds, while warning that AI-assisted mathematical breakthroughs could also challenge some lattice-based cryptography.
title: Ethereum Researcher Cautions AI Could Threaten Crypto Wallet Security

description: The European Securities and Markets Authority has told MiCA-authorised crypto-asset service providers to stop offering services related to stablecoins that do not meet MiCA requirements. New purchases, trading, promotion, and distribution of affected tokens must stop.
title: ESMA Orders Crypto Firms to Exit Non-Compliant Stablecoins Within Three Months

description: Google has expanded access to its SynthID Detector, allowing users to check digital media for invisible watermarks associated with AI-generated content. The tool was previously aimed at media professionals but is now available globally in English. It supports watermarks created by Google and participating AI companies, including OpenAI, Nvidia and Kakao, with Apple support coming soon. Google introduced SynthID in 2023 and says it has watermarked more than 180 billion images and videos, as well as 240,000 years' worth of audio.
title: Google Rolls Out SynthID Detector Globally for AI-Generated Images, Videos and Audio

description: Anthropic on Thursday announced Claude Haiku 5.5 as its fastest model to date. The company says it is aimed at developers running high-volume and cost-sensitive AI workloads. Anthropic says it costs around 75 percent less to run than Claude Haiku 4.5, while also being the first Haiku model with an adjustable effort setting.
title: Anthropic Launches Claude Haiku 5.5 as Faster, Cheaper Model for High-Volume AI Tasks

description: Google on Wednesday announced Playground as an experimental gaming platform. As per the Mountain View-based tech giant, it lets users create, play, and share custom browser-based games using natural-language prompts. They can start with a blank canvas or remix prompts, then describe changes to gameplay, characters, physics, and environments through a conversational interface. Apart from this, Google is preparing a deeper integration with Unity Spark, adding further capabilities to Playground.
title: Google Labs Playground Turns AI Prompts Into Playable Games Without Any Coding
